name: IL-10
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Brad Schneider running with large financial advantage ($3.0M raised, $1.7M on hand)
Republican challenger Carl Lambrecht has no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~96%
model.rationale: The D+12 district, Schneider's incumbency and overwhelming fundraising edge, and a little-known, unfunded Republican challenger all point to a safe Democratic hold, with markets agreeing at roughly 96%.
model.watch: A major polling surprise or unexpected outside spending against Schneider would be the main signal of a tighter race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Brad Schneider seeks another term in a northern Illinois district that leans twelve points Democratic. He enters with a large war chest of about $1.7 million on hand and no meaningful outside opposition, while Republican Carl Lambrecht reports no fundraising activity. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the picture rests on district fundamentals and money.

Prediction markets give Schneider roughly a 96% chance of winning, consistent with the seat's partisan lean and his incumbency. The expected margin is about twenty-one points, with elevated uncertainty because direct polling evidence is absent. Any surprise would likely come from a late influx of outside spending or a polling shock, neither of which currently appears on the horizon.
